analysis: Aminoglycosides are known to be ototoxic and primarily affect the outer hair cells in the cochlea. The evidence indicates that the most significant damage occurs in the basal area of the cochlea, where outer hair cells are more vulnerable to the toxic effects of these antibiotics. While inner hair cells can also be affected, the predominant impact of aminoglycosides is on the outer hair cells, particularly in the basal region. Therefore, the best-supported option is that aminoglycosides affect the outer hair cells in the basal area.
